correctness.rationale: Strict convexity and two conjugate-linear isometries force the unique complex minimizer to have reciprocal real quadratic residual. The derivative of its scalar arcsine integral has opposite signs at a=1/4 and a=1/2, giving a unique stationary point for every p>1. The proof of the large-p law rederives the exact positive and negative endpoint substitutions and gamma integrals: P~(2 sqrt(2pi))^-1 (bp)^-3/2 and N~sqrt(2/pi) L^(p-1/2)(bp)^-1/2. Their stationarity balance is L^(p-1/2)~1/(4bp), which yields 4p(1/2-a)=log(4p)+o(1) and the root law. The positive endpoint of F_p is asymptotically (2pi bp)^-1/2 and the negative endpoint is O(p^-3/2), proving the moment law for all real p tending to infinity. The exact p=2 solution and finite computational checks p=2..400 match; computation is supplementary, not an infinite proof. See RESULT.md and checks/check.py.

value.rationale: For the explicitly studied canonical generator f=1-z, finite-p approximate zeros appear already in Centner Example 6.4, motivating the sharp quantitative question of their unit-circle approach as p increases. The result gives the first fixed-degree exponent-asymptotic benchmark within the inspected same-object literature: an unexpected logarithmic-over-linear layer, explicit constant 4, and sharp residual p-moment 1/sqrt(2pi p). These precise quantities are not generic consequences of a uniqueness theorem or fixed-p tables; they require an endpoint-dominated balance between polynomial and exponentially small terms and can guide rate questions for related nonlinear Hardy projection examples. No broader theorem or future citation impact is claimed. In particular the coefficientwise limiting residual (1+z^2)/2 has p-th moment ~sqrt(2/(pi p)), twice the optimal p-th moment: asymptotic minimization and substitution of the limiting residual do not commute at the leading moment coefficient.
